Plant Manager – Precast Manufacturing
Location:
Greater Lubbock, TX Area
Compensation:
$165,000 – $200,000 Base Salary + Bonus + Excellent Benefits
About the Opportunity
Enhanced Staffing is recruiting for a Plant Manager to lead the startup, operational buildout, and long-term production leadership of a new state-of-the-art precast manufacturing facility currently being developed in the Forth Worth area.
This facility will support the rapidly growing data center construction market throughout the Southwest and nationally, supplying structural and architectural precast systems for hyperscale and mission-critical infrastructure projects.
This is a high-impact executive leadership opportunity for a proven manufacturing operations leader who thrives in building teams, driving operational excellence, and scaling production within complex industrial environments.
Position Summary
The Plant Manager will oversee all aspects of plant operations including production, safety, quality, maintenance, staffing, scheduling, budgeting, and continuous improvement initiatives. The ideal candidate will bring strong leadership experience within precast concrete, heavy manufacturing, structural concrete, or industrial production environments.
This individual will work closely with executive leadership, engineering, project management, quality, and field operations teams to ensure the facility operates safely, efficiently, and at the highest quality standards while supporting aggressive growth in the data center sector.
Responsibilities
Lead startup and operational execution of a new precast manufacturing facility
Build and develop high-performing production, maintenance, and operations teams
Oversee daily plant operations including production, scheduling, quality, safety, maintenance, and logistics
Drive operational efficiency, productivity improvements, and continuous improvement initiatives
Establish KPIs and operational metrics for plant performance, labor utilization, throughput, and quality
Ensure compliance with OSHA, environmental, and company safety standards
Manage plant staffing, workforce planning, training, and employee development
Collaborate with engineering and project teams to support production planning and delivery schedules
Oversee maintenance strategies for equipment reliability and facility uptime
Manage operational budgets, forecasting, and cost controls
Support manufacturing scalability to meet growing demand from hyperscale and mission-critical data center projects
Foster a culture of accountability, teamwork, safety, and operational excellence
Partner with executive leadership on long-term operational strategy and facility growth
Qualifications
10+ years of manufacturing leadership experience in precast concrete, concrete products, steel fabrication, industrial manufacturing, or heavy production environments
Prior Plant Manager, Operations Manager, Manufacturing Manager, or Senior Production leadership experience required
Strong experience managing large production teams in fast-paced manufacturing operations
Experience with startup facilities, plant expansions, or greenfield operations strongly preferred
Knowledge of precast concrete manufacturing processes highly preferred
Experience supporting large-scale construction, infrastructure, industrial, or mission-critical projects preferred
Strong operational leadership, budgeting, staffing, and process improvement background
Proven ability to drive safety, quality, and production performance
Excellent communication and leadership skills
Lean manufacturing or continuous improvement experience is a plus
Compensation & Benefits
$160,000 – $200,000 base salary
Performance-based bonus program
Excellent medical, dental, and vision benefits
401(k) with company contribution
PTO and paid holidays
Long-term growth opportunity with a rapidly expanding organization
Opportunity to play a key leadership role in a major strategic expansion initiative
Industry Focus
This facility will support some of the most advanced and rapidly growing data center developments in North America, manufacturing structural and architectural precast systems for hyperscale and mission-critical infrastructure projects.

Director of Manufacturing
No longer accepting applications
Freestyle Snacks
Atlanta Metropolitan Area
Director of Manufacturing & Commercialization
Location: Remote, with regular travel to production facilities
About Freestyle Snacks
At Freestyle Snacks, we're building the future of savory snacking. We take bold, flavorful olives and pickles from the best growing regions in the world and reinvent them in convenient, mess-free packaging that fits seamlessly into modern life, creating an entirely new way to snack on foods people already know and love.
Since launching in 2022, Freestyle has expanded to more than 7,000 retail locations nationwide, including Whole Foods, Target, Walmart, Costco, and Delta Air Lines. We're growing quickly and looking for ambitious, curious people who are energized by hard problems, happy getting their hands dirty, and hungry for real ownership.
About the Role
Freestyle Snacks is seeking a Director of Manufacturing & Commercialization to own how we make our products and how new ones get to market. This is not a compliance or paperwork role.
We produce through partner facilities in the U.S. and abroad, and our biggest constraints are capacity, cost of goods, consistency, and speed to market on new items. This role owns all four. The day-to-day is managing our co-manufacturers, quality, and food safety. The longer-term work is commercialization: you’ll make the team’s new product ideas come to life by challenging co-manufacturer recommendations, exploring alternatives, and landing on the best, most cost-effective solution. You'll have project management support on launches, so your focus is on execution.
You should be comfortable walking a plant floor, reading a costing model, and pushing back on a supplier in the same week. A background in food science or R&D is a plus. You will work directly with the Founder & CEO and partner closely with operations, finance, sales, and marketing.
What You'll Do
Own and Scale the Manufacturing Network
Own the co-manufacturing network as primary point of contact, from day-to-day communication through weekly calls, QBRs, and on-site production oversight.
Build the capacity plan for our growth, and source and qualify new partners so no single facility is a point of failure.
Run partner scorecards on RFT, OTIF, cost per pound, yield, and complaint rate, and hold facilities to agreed standards and corrective action timelines.
Build relationships strong enough that partners flag problems early and prioritize us when capacity is tight, and represent their capabilities and constraints inside Freestyle.
Partner with operations on production planning, lead times, MOQs, and inventory strategy.
Communicate early and honestly when an issue will affect supply, cost, or a customer commitment.
Evaluate equipment, automation, and capital investment opportunities to improve manufacturing capacity, efficiency, and cost.
Lead Commercialization
Execute the commercialization of new products, line extensions, and formats, from concept through trials, scale-up, and first commercial run.
Translate concepts into specs and feasibility assessments with our manufacturing partners.
Challenge co-manufacturer recommendations and explore alternative processes, formats, packaging, ingredients, and partners to find the best, most cost-effective path.
Own benchtop work, plant trials, costing, packaging development, and shelf-life and food safety validation for new items, and make the go/no-go call on technical readiness.
Work alongside the project lead on each launch, providing technical input on timelines, flagging risks early, and delivering your workstreams on schedule.
Negotiate Cost Savings
Negotiate co-manufacturing rates, tolling agreements, and contract terms, plus ingredient and packaging supply through competitive bids where it makes sense.
Find savings through run size, formulation, packaging design, case pack, and freight.
Lead SKU rationalization based on complexity, margin, and velocity.
Deliver measurable, year-over-year margin improvement without compromising quality.
Drive Performance and Quality
Own specs and finished goods standards for every SKU, and lead projects that improve throughput and quality while reducing cost.
Lead root cause analysis and corrective action for service and quality failures, and catch risks before they reach a customer.
Track consumer complaint trends by lot, facility, and production date and close the loop on root cause.
Ensure partners maintain the food safety programs, certifications, and documentation our customers require, including during retailer onboarding.
Who You Are
5+ years in food manufacturing, R&D, commercialization, or operations, ideally in CPG.
Hands-on experience managing co-manufacturers (not just internal plants), including sourcing partners, structuring agreements, and negotiating real, quantified cost savings.
Direct experience commercializing food products with co-manufacturers from concept through first production run, with the technical depth to challenge their recommendations and propose credible alternatives.
Fluent in COGS, unit economics, and metrics like OTIF, yield, and cost per pound, and you use them to run relationships, not just report them.
Enough food safety and quality knowledge to write a spec, read an audit, and hold a plant accountable. No QA certification required.
Calm under pressure and rigorous about root cause. You follow through until the fix holds.
Thrives in a startup: comfortable building the system while operating it, moving with urgency, and making sound decisions with imperfect information.
Clear communicator who can turn technical and cost issues into recommendations for a non-technical team.
Willing to be on the plant floor and travel ~30–40%, including internationally.
Why Join Freestyle?
Join one of the fastest growing brands in the category and make an outsized impact on its trajectory.
Healthcare benefits, 401(k), flexible PTO, and professional development opportunities.
Unlimited olives and pickles.
If you would like to be considered for this role please send your resume to ally@freestylesnacking.com

capture.text:
Vice President, Quality
nVent
St Louis Park, MN
We’re looking for people who put their innovation to work to advance our success – and their own. Join an organization that ensures a more secure world through connecting and protecting our customers with inventive electrical solutions.
The Vice President of Quality is an enterprise leadership role accountable for enterprise quality performance, not just quality systems. This leader will define and execute nVent’s quality strategy across the full value chain, with direct accountability for improving customer escapes, cost of poor quality, first-pass yield, supplier quality performance, warranty performance, product reliability, on-time-to-customer impact, and launch quality. The role will shift quality from a primarily compliance- and governance-centered function to a performance-driving enterprise capability that improves customer outcomes, operational execution, and business growth.
Reporting to the Chief Supply Chain Officer, the Vice President Quality will serve as the senior-most quality leader for nVent, setting the vision, operating model, performance expectations, capabilities, and accountability mechanisms required to scale quality as nVent grows. This leader will partner closely with segment presidents, operations, engineering, product management, sourcing and procurement, digital, commercial, legal, and finance leaders to embed quality into business decision-making and deliver measurable improvements in customer experience, reliability, warranty, launch readiness, supplier performance, operational quality, and quality-related business risk.
What You Will Experience In This Position
Enterprise Quality Performance and Accountability
Own enterprise quality performance outcomes, including customer escapes, cost of poor quality, first-pass yield, supplier quality, warranty, reliability, launch quality, and the impact of quality issues on on-time-to-customer performance.
Translate quality strategy into measurable business results, ensuring quality priorities are directly connected to customer experience, operational performance, growth, profitability, and risk reduction.
Establish clear enterprise, segment, region, business unit, and site-level accountability for the quality metrics that matter most to customers and the business.
Lead operating reviews that move beyond reporting activity to identifying performance gaps, driving root cause ownership, and sustaining measurable improvement.
New Product Quality and Launch Excellence
Elevate new product quality as a core enterprise capability, ensuring quality is designed into high-growth platforms, strategic programs, and critical infrastructure solutions from concept through launch and field performance.
Partner with engineering, product management, operations, and commercial leaders to strengthen quality planning, design validation, process validation, risk assessment, reliability requirements, and launch readiness across major programs such as Saturn, Avatar, Data Solutions growth initiatives, and other strategic launches.
Ensure robust NPI quality gates, readiness reviews, and escalation criteria are in place to prevent launch defects, customer escapes, warranty exposure, and reliability issues.
Build feedback loops from field performance, warranty, customer quality, and manufacturing quality data into product development and launch processes.
Digital Quality, Analytics, and Enterprise Quality Intelligence
Lead the evolution of digital quality as an enterprise capability, including predictive quality, AI-enabled risk detection, manufacturing quality analytics, digital traceability, and enterprise quality intelligence.
Partner with Digital and Integrated Supply Chain leaders to modernize eQMS capabilities, automate quality workflows, strengthen data integrity, and establish a single source of truth for enterprise quality performance.
Use advanced analytics to identify leading indicators of quality risk across product design, suppliers, manufacturing processes, field performance, warranty, and customer experience.
Move the organization from lagging quality reporting to predictive and preventive insights that enable faster decisions, better prioritization, and measurable performance improvement.
Quality Management Systems, Compliance, and Standards
Lead the modernization, standardization, and continuous improvement of nVent’s Quality Management System, ensuring systems and standards enable performance improvement rather than becoming ends in themselves.
Ensure readiness and sustained compliance with applicable quality and regulatory standards, including ISO 9001 and other business-relevant standards such as ISO 14001, AS9100, customer-specific requirements, and regional regulatory expectations.
Strengthen management review, internal audit, external audit, and corrective and preventive action processes to ensure systemic issues are identified, resolved, and prevented from recurring.
Partner with legal, compliance, engineering, operations, and commercial teams to manage quality-related risk and ensure quality commitments are understood, objective, and executable.
Customer, Supplier, and Operational Quality
Build customer quality capability that improves responsiveness, transparency, containment, corrective action effectiveness, customer confidence, and reduction of repeat escapes.
Advance supplier quality strategy, qualification, audit discipline, scorecards, supplier development, and escalation processes to improve supplier performance and protect customer commitments.
Embed quality into manufacturing and operational processes with a focus on defect prevention, first-pass yield, process capability, reliability, error proofing, and flow to customer.
Use customer feedback, warranty data, supplier performance, manufacturing quality, field performance, and operational metrics to prioritize systemic improvement opportunities.
Leadership, Talent, and Quality Culture
Champion a quality-first culture where leaders model prevention-based decision-making and teams are empowered to stop, escalate, and resolve issues before they reach the customer.
Build, develop, and inspire a high-performing quality leadership team with clear accountability, succession depth, and strong capability across enterprise, segment, regional, and site quality roles.
Lead through influence in a matrixed environment, balancing enterprise standards with business-specific execution needs and measurable performance outcomes.
Model executive leadership behaviors, including strategic thinking, courageous decision-making, stakeholder engagement, talent development, collaboration, adaptability, and self-accountability.
You Have
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, quality, operations, supply chain, business, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
15+ years of progressive quality, operations, engineering, or supply chain leadership experience in a global manufacturing environment, including significant leadership of multi-site or enterprise quality functions.
Demonstrated experience improving quality performance outcomes, including customer escapes, cost of poor quality, first-pass yield, supplier quality, warranty, reliability, and launch quality.
Strong experience in new product quality, design validation, process validation, launch readiness, reliability engineering, and quality risk management for complex product portfolios.
Experience advancing digital quality capabilities, including eQMS, quality analytics, digital traceability, predictive insights, and AI-enabled risk detection.
Proven ability to lead enterprise-level change across a complex, matrixed, global organization.
Exceptional communication, influencing, and executive presence, with the ability to translate quality priorities into business value.
Willingness to travel domestically and internationally as required.
Suggested Success Measures
Reduced customer escapes and repeat quality issues, with improved containment, responsiveness, and corrective action effectiveness.
Improved cost of poor quality, first-pass yield, process capability, reliability, warranty performance, and on-time-to-customer impact from quality issues.
Improved supplier quality performance through stronger qualification, development, governance, scorecards, and corrective action discipline.
Stronger new product quality outcomes, including improved launch readiness, fewer launch defects, reduced warranty exposure, and better reliability performance.
Expanded digital quality maturity, including predictive quality insights, AI-enabled risk detection, digital traceability, and enterprise quality intelligence.
Increased quality maturity from reactive issue management to proactive prevention, measurable performance improvement, and stronger enterprise accountability.
We Have
A dynamic global reach with diverse operations around the world that will stretch your abilities, provide plentiful career opportunities, and allow you to make an impact every day
nVent is a leading global provider of electrical connection and protection solutions. We believe our inventive electrical solutions enable safer systems and ensure a more secure world. We design, manufacture, market, install and service high performance products and solutions that connect and protect some of the world's most sensitive equipment, buildings and critical processes. We offer a comprehensive range of systems protection and electrical connections solutions across industry-leading brands that are recognized globally for quality, reliability and innovation.
Our principal office is in London and our management office in the United States is in Minneapolis. Our robust portfolio of leading electrical product brands dates back more than 100 years and includes nVent CADDY, ERICO, HOFFMAN, ILSCO, SCHROFF and TRACHTE. Learn more at www.nvent.com.
Commitment to strengthen communities where our employees live and work
We encourage and support the philanthropic activities of our employees worldwide
Through our nVent in Action matching program, we provide funds to nonprofit and educational organizations where our employees volunteer or donate money
Core values that shape our culture and drive us to deliver the best for our employees and our customers. We’re known for being:
Innovative & adaptable
Dedicated to absolute integrity
Focused on the customer first
Respectful and team oriented
Optimistic and energizing
Accountable for performance
Benefits to support the lives of our employees
Pay Transparency
nVent’s pay scale is based on the expected range of base pay for this job and the employee’s work location. Employee pay within this range will be based on a combination of factors including knowledge, skills, abilities, experience, education, and performance. Where federal, state, or local minimum wage requirements exist, employee pay will comply.
Compensation Range
$241,500.00 - $359,000.00
Depending on the position offered, employee may be eligible for other forms of compensation, such as annual incentives.
Benefit Overview
At nVent, we value our people and their health and well-being. We provide a broad benefits package with meaningful programs for eligible full-time employees that includes:
Medical, dental, and vision plans along with flexible spending accounts, short-term and long-term disability benefits, critical illness, accident insurance and life insurance.
A 401(k) retirement plan and an employee stock purchase plan — both include a company match.
Other supplemental benefits may include tuition reimbursement, caregiver, personal and parental leave, back-up care services, paid time off including volunteer time, a well-being program, and/or legal & identity theft protection.
At nVent, we connect and protect our customers with inventive electrical solutions. People are our most valuable asset. Inclusion and diversity means that we celebrate and encourage each other’s authenticity because we understand that uniqueness sparks growth.

Director Quality
Thermo Fisher Scientific
Middletown, VA
Work Schedule
Standard (Mon-Fri)
Environmental Conditions
Office
As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.
As Director of Quality and Compliance,
you will be responsible for taking a transformative approach to leading a dynamic and high-functioning Quality Assurance team at the Thermo Fisher Scientific, Clinical Diagnostics Division site in Middletown VA
The successful candidate will be responsible for raising the bar in process and culture across all aspects of quality system and compliance at the location, which performs development and manufacture of IVD products in adherence to applicable global regulations and standards such as US FDA QMSR, IVDD / IVDR, ISO13485:2016 (under MDSAP) and other GMP standards.
You will have responsibility for advising and collaborating with Manufacturing, Technical Operation and Commercial functions on quality and quality system requirements to ensure activities remain in compliance, and for driving continued evolution of the Quality function and site quality system to ensure it remains adequate to business needs and is successfully implemented.
This is a highly visible role at the site and Division level and, as a key member of the leadership team, you will report to the CDD Vice President, Global Quality Assurance & Regulatory Affairs.
A critical aspect of this role is serving as the primary quality representative for customers and regulatory authorities. As the site's Management Representative, the Director is responsible for ensuring the effectiveness of the Quality Management System and leading interactions during FDA inspections, MDSAP and ISO 13485 audits, and customer audits. This role requires strong leadership and communication skills to build customer confidence, maintain regulatory compliance, and represent Thermo Fisher Scientific with credibility and professionalism.
Key Responsibilities:
Acts as Management Representative of the Quality System and official correspondent of the site to all regulators (including US FDA). Primary contact at the site for all audits (regulator, Notified Body and customer).
Serve as a member of the site leadership team, providing strategic direction and influencing business decisions to ensure quality, compliance, and operational excellence are integrated into site objectives.
Establish strategies and drives actions to ensure the Quality Management System is adequate and successfully implemented to remain in sustained compliance with applicable regulations and standards.
Responsible for site product quality, compliance, conformance to quality requirements and specifications, and customer quality requirements. Supports regulatory recalls and interaction with government agencies.
Directly interacts with customers and OEM partners in relation to quality agreements, and quality matters associated with provided products and services.
Champion risk-based decision making by overseeing quality risk management processes and ensuring risks are identified, assessed, mitigated, and monitored throughout the product lifecycle.
Attracts, develops, and retains top talent to build an outstanding quality / regulatory function. Implements the required interpersonal structures and operating mechanisms to maintain appropriate oversight of the compliance status of the business and achieve results.
Grows and develops a customer-focused culture of personal quality in all site functions through leading, educating, and motivating site personnel using industry-leading practices.
Establishes and leads annual personnel resource and financial plans for the quality / regulatory organization.
Establishes annual site quality goals and objectives as part of annual Quality Improvement Plan and develops strategies and tactics to deliver associated results.
Leads and participates in cross functional teams for new product development, technology transfer, process improvement, and general operations.
Partners with regulatory affairs in all aspects of site regulatory processes that ensure the appropriate licensing, marketing and legal compliance of all appropriate diagnostics and medical device products globally.
Collaborate with global Quality and Regulatory leadership to standardize best practices, share lessons learned, and support enterprise quality initiatives.
Minimum Requirements/Qualifications:
A minimum of 10 years of quality / regulatory experience including at least 5 years of prior experience leading a quality / regulatory role.
Undergraduate degree in life science or biomedical engineering-related subject area preferred.
Strong demonstration of leadership capabilities required, with experience in driving organization and process change. Experience in leading transformations is preferred.
Strong solid understanding of QMS standards and medical device requirements/regulations (ISO 13485:2016 (preferably under MDSAP), US FDA QMSR, Health Canada, IVDD / IVDR)
Experienced in direct, professional interactions with customers and OEM business partners and regulatory authorities.
Ability to achieve results in a matrixed organization, using representatives from diverse cultures and embracing diversity.
Travel requirement:
<10% regional and international travel is expected.
Compensation And Benefits
The salary range estimated for this position based in Virginia is $145,500.00–$225,000.00.
This position may also be eligible to receive a variable annual bonus based on company, team, and/or individual performance results in accordance with company policy. We offer a comprehensive Total Rewards package that our U.S. colleagues and their families can count on, which includes:
A choice of national medical and dental plans, and a national vision plan, including health incentive programs
Employee assistance and family support programs, including commuter benefits and tuition reimbursement
At least 120 hours paid time off (PTO), 10 paid holidays annually, paid parental leave (3 weeks for bonding and 8 weeks for caregiver leave), accident and life insurance, and short- and long-term disability in accordance with company policy
Retirement and savings programs, such as our competitive 401(k) U.S. retirement savings plan
Employees’ Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offers eligible colleagues the opportunity to purchase company stock at a discount

capture.text:
Sr. Director - API Manufacturing Quality Assurance
BioSpace
Huntsville, AL
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.
Lilly is currently constructing an advanced manufacturing facility for production of API molecules. This facility is intended to provide APIs for current and future products, including new modalities. This is a unique opportunity to be a part of the leadership team for the startup of a greenfield manufacturing site, and the successful candidate will help to build the organization, the facility and the culture to enable a successful startup into GMP manufacturing operations.
Position Overview
The Sr. Director – QA serves as the Site Quality Leader for the Lilly API site, overseeing manufacturing, utilities, laboratories, and warehousing. This role ensures the strength and continuous improvement of all quality and compliance systems, activities, and personnel. Additionally, the Sr. Director – QA is responsible for maintaining utilities and ensuring that raw materials and drug substances are produced and released in accordance with cGMP standards and marketing authorization requirements.
Key Responsibilities
Serve as Site Quality Leader on the Lilly Site Lead Team.
Ensure site-wide compliance with cGMPs, procedures, standards, and regulatory commitments.
Lead the API Quality Team and manage its agenda.
Support quality forums (e.g., Deviation and Change Control Boards).
Develop and monitor a site Quality Plan and metrics.
Coordinate and manage regulatory inspections.
Review and approve manufacturing and quality system documents.
Ensure adequate QA staffing and provide coaching and development.
Use HR tools for performance management, staffing, and succession planning.
Contribute to QA business planning and site-wide strategic planning.
Basic Requirements

Renesas Electronics

The Senior Director of Test & Product Engineering leads the strategy and execution of test and product engineering for power semiconductor modules, power ICs, and controllers supporting data center and high-performance applications. This role owns end-to-end product execution across characterization, qualification, yield ramp, test development, and high-volume manufacturing. The leader ensures delivery of scalable, cost-competitive, and high-quality products through strong cross-functional alignment with Design, Product Line, Quality, Reliability, and Operations.
Job Description
The role defines and executes a unified strategy across test and product engineering while leading global teams and establishing scalable processes for new product introduction, yield ramp, and sustaining operations. It requires a balance of strategic leadership and hands-on execution to drive predictable delivery and continuous improvement.
From a product engineering perspective, this leader owns the full product lifecycle, including silicon bring-up, qualification, ramp, and sustaining. Responsibilities include driving yield ramp and improvement, managing excursions, and optimizing product cost through yield, test efficiency, and manufacturing performance. The role ensures manufacturing readiness, production stability, and resolution of yield issues across fab, assembly, and test. It also owns product KPIs, manages change control processes (ECO/PCN), and partners with design teams on design-for-yield, parametric margining, and specification alignment.
From a test engineering standpoint, the role leads development and deployment of wafer sort, final test, and characterization solutions, ensuring strong test coverage while optimizing cost and efficiency. Responsibilities include driving test time reduction, multisite efficiency, and ATE platform standardization to enable scalable high-volume manufacturing.
The leader is accountable for resolving yield excursions, test escapes, and customer returns while partnering with Quality and Reliability teams to ensure robust qualification and mission-profile alignment. This includes establishing monitoring systems and controls to proactively manage risk and maintain alignment between product performance, test limits, and reliability targets.
The role works closely with Operations and manufacturing partners to ensure production readiness, capacity alignment, and continuous improvement across internal and OSAT sites. Strong cross-functional collaboration is required to align with Design, Product Line, and Applications teams on methodologies, cost targets, and customer requirements.
From a business standpoint, the Senior Director owns budget, headcount, and capital planning, while driving performance against key metrics such as yield, cost, quality, and cycle time. The role is also responsible for building a strong organization through hiring, development, and succession planning.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or related field (advanced degree preferred) with 15+ years of semiconductor experience across test and/or product engineering, including leadership of global teams. Strong technical background in power semiconductors (Si, SiC, GaN, modules, or power ICs) and a proven track record in yield ramp, cost optimization, and high-volume manufacturing execution are required. Deep understanding of ATE, characterization, and yield analysis, along with experience driving cross-functional execution across the full product lifecycle, is essential.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with data center power architectures (AC-DC, DC-DC) and familiarity with power module packaging, thermal behavior, and high-current test methods are preferred. Additional strengths include statistical yield analysis, reliability and qualification methodologies, and experience with test automation and data analytics in manufacturing environments.
Key Performance Indicators
Success in this role is measured by yield performance and improvement, cost of test reduction, product cost competitiveness, execution of NPI and ramp schedules, product quality and reliability, and improvements in cycle time and manufacturing efficiency.
What Success Looks Like
Success is defined by consistent product ramps with strong yield, quality, and cost performance, supported by predictable execution from development through production. The organization demonstrates rapid resolution of yield and quality issues and is recognized as a key driver of product competitiveness and customer satisfaction.

Renesas is an embedded semiconductor solution provider driven by its Purpose, To Make Our Lives Easier

Oversees implementation, adapts, and stays up to date with organizational change, challenges, feedback, best practices, processes, and industry trends; shares best practices within and across teams. Fosters open dialogue amongst team members, engages, motivates, and promotes collaboration within and across teams; motivates teams to meet business objectives. Head of Hardware
No longer accepting applications
Workshop Venture Partners
Austin, TX
About Drover
Drover is building a virtual fencing ear tag for cattle, and the platform around it to run the modern ranch.
Fencing is one of the oldest unsolved problems in agriculture. Ranchers spend billions of dollars a year building and maintaining physical fences, and every fence line locks land into a grazing pattern it wasn't made for. Virtual fencing is changing that, a generational shift in how ranches are run, bringing precision and productivity gains to an industry that has to feed a growing population with fewer resources.
But every system on the market today requires a collar: bulky, infrastructure-dependent, and built around electric shock. We're taking a path the industry thought impossible. We've shrunk virtual fencing into the ear tag, the form factor every cattle producer on earth already uses. Our tag combines low-power GPS, cellular and satellite connectivity, embedded sensing, solar power, and patent-pending muscle stimulation that guides cattle directionally rather than shocking them. Ranchers tag their cattle once and immediately start running their operation from their phone.
We were founded by Callum Taylor (Harvard, EE & fifth-generation ranching family) and Samuel Aubin (USYD, CS), who both grew up in Australian ranching towns. We built a working ear tag and a patent-pending stimulation method in twelve months (five times faster than competitors), and are now scaling manufacturing to put the technology on every head of cattle in the USA, Australia, and New Zealand.
We closed an oversubscribed seed round, signed a top-tier contract manufacturer, and are on track to launch commercially in Texas in Q1 2027.
We're headquartered in Austin, Texas.
About The Role
As Head of Hardware, you will lead all hardware development at Drover: taking our first-generation ear tag from design validation through production, standing up our supply chain and quality systems with our contract manufacturer, and shaping the roadmap for what comes next.
We're an early-stage startup. You'll have high ownership in what you build and the direction of future generations of our product. You'll own the device end-to-end, electronics, power, RF, mechanical integration, and the path to volume manufacturing, and work directly with the founders on scaling the hardware to cattle globally. As Drover scales, you'll build and lead the hardware engineering team.
What You'll Do
Own Drover hardware across the company. Set the technical direction for current and future generations of the product, and hire the team to build them
Drive manufacturing through EVT, DVT, and PVT, ensuring design maturity, test coverage, and release readiness at each gate
Lead electrical design and review across the full system: cellular and satellite connectivity, GNSS, power management and solar harvesting, embedded sensing, and our patent-pending low-voltage muscle stimulation circuit
Travel overseas to work hands-on with our contract manufacturer on DFM, test fixtures, yield, and production ramp for commercial launch
Work with our liaisons to build and manage the supply chain
Establish quality assurance and reliability testing for a device that has to survive years on a cow's ear in the sun, rain, and mud
Drive regulatory and certification work (FCC, CE, RCM, carrier certification, battery transport and safety)
Opportunity to work from our field offices located within an hour of Austin to prototype and review product iterations on working ranches
Requirements
5+ years as an electrical engineer, with at least one product taken from prototype to volume production
2+ years of leadership experience, and willing to hire and manage a team of engineers
Strong PCB design skills, including schematic capture, layout review, and lab debugging
Experience working with contract manufacturers and managing a hardware supply chain
Solid understanding of low-power embedded systems: battery-powered devices, power budgeting, energy harvesting
Comfortable guiding product development and product iteration cycles in a fast-paced environment
Willing to work in-person in Austin, TX
Nice to have
IoT, wearable, or asset-tracking products, especially rugged or outdoor devices
RF design and test experience: cellular modems, GNSS, antenna design
Mechanical and enclosure experience: mechanical design, injection moulding, ingress protection, environmental testing
Firmware fluency (Zephyr, nRF Connect, or similar) and comfort reading and debugging embedded code
Agricultural or livestock background, or a willingness to get to know our customers
Note: Even if you don't have all of the above and still think you're an excellent candidate, please reach out. We're always open to great people with core skillsets who are willing to push and learn.
Benefits
Meaningful equity package with a high trajectory start-up
Health, dental, vision insurance
Paid family and medical leave
Unlimited PTO
Collaborative environment with emphasis on strong team culture
Ownership and responsibility

capture.text:
Quality Control Technician - I
TestEquity LLC
Houston, Texas
Description
Summary/Purpose of the Position:
The Quality Control Technician I is responsible for performing quality control reviews of purchased and/or manufactured products and records. This activity is executed in real-time and in accordance with the Quality System guidelines.
Essential Duties, Functions and/or Responsibilities:
Performs incoming, first articles, in-process, final inspection, and re-work quality checks, using a wide variety of inspection tools.
Determine product acceptance status after inspection.
Identifies and escalates non-conformances observed during inspection.
Follow Good Documentation Practices (GDP) during document review and inspection.
Performs all work in compliance with company policy and within the guidelines.
Ensures process compliance, as needed/required.
Reviews and approves production batch records (i.e., Device History records).
Releases work in process to finished goods inventory. Flags inconsistent or incorrect records and report errors to supervisors or the management team.
Inspects products to specification or processes.
Segregates non-confirming product and seeks guidance on reporting the non-conformance.
Physically quarantines non-conforming products and seeks guidance on reporting the quarantined materials.
Performs QC testing as needed.
Exhibits competence with testing methods selected for assigned tasks.
Maintains a safe and healthy work environment by following standards and procedures, complying with legal regulations.
Reports Quality problems or concerns to direct reports or the quality manager.
Populates databases for collection and analysis.
Directly and indirectly responsible for product quality
Other duties as assigned.
Qualifications
Education and/or Work Experience Requirements:
High School Diploma or GED required.
Quality related field, manufacturing, regulated industry experience is preferred
Ability to operate basic measuring tools such as calipers or micrometers is required
Knowledge of quality test methods and use of related lab equipment is preferred
Working knowledge of general accident prevention practices
Basic Math skills is required
Resourceful, analytical, organized, and inquisitive
Strong interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills
Knowledge of Office Software - Microsoft Excel, Word, Outlook and PowerPoint
Attention to detail and quality and safety conscious
High level of urgency
Physical Requirements:
Ability to safely and successfully perform essential job functions in accordance with the ADA, FMLA, and other federal, state, and local standards, including meeting qualitative and/or quantitative productivity standards.
Ability to maintain regular and timely attendance in accordance with the ADA, FMLA, and other federal, state, and local regulations.
Ability to lift up to 50 lbs. when necessary.
This position requires applicants to be authorized to work in the US without sponsorship; TestEquity does not sponsor applicants for work visas.
TestEquity provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.
This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.
